memoryReview.evidence: apps/picto/visual-direction.json and app.js inspected; shared typographic tray of pictograms.
memoryReview.lesson: Do not reuse typewriter paper or pictographic grammar; use toy objects, color, personal handouts.
Avoid paintings in ornate museum frames and any retouching metaphor.
Distinguish all color and spacing from tape-recorder workspaces.

references.observation: Memphis design uses contrasting bright colors and deliberately unexpected object configurations.
references.principle: Clashing hues become playful when large silhouette blocks organize the composition.
references.application: Large saturated orange and yellow stage elements with dark structural geometry.
references.avoid: No direct reproductions of Memphis products or iconic designer patterns.

references.observation: A small historical toy theatre builds scenes from moveable print elements at different depths.
references.principle: The composition can be assembled from independently manipulated objects.
references.application: Direct finger positioning of SVG silhouettes, deliberate stacking order and visible object tray.
references.avoid: Do not replicate the museum's Cinderella illustration, wooden frame or staging.

references.observation: Surreal descriptions create funny drawings that are judged by other players.
references.principle: The fun lies in the interpretation, not merely dexterity of drawing.
references.application: Curated varied absurd prompts, simultaneous creation and masked voting.
references.avoid: No copies of Drawful visuals, drawing interface, prompts or answer-submission mechanic.

concepts.medium: Original stroke-drawn SVG plastic toy silhouettes with eight category inks and five overlay mutations.
concepts.composition: Large square free scene and a horizontal mobile prop tray; dark set-like header.
concepts.interaction: Choose an item, place it, drag/flip/rotate/change layer, secretly publish then vote.
concepts.motion: Firm physical depressions, a brief snap on creation, no idle visual effects.
concepts.rationale: Fits online party tempo and differs materially from paper, museum and audio projects.

concepts.medium: Carved stone reliefs and monochrome contour plates.
concepts.composition: Round gallery with radial inventory and central mosaic circles.
concepts.interaction: Snapped placement into repeated concentric rings.
concepts.motion: Slow carved-block slides with heavy dust clouds.
concepts.rationale: Too constrained for arbitrary spatial jokes and tedious on touchscreens.

concepts.medium: VHS phosphor and halftone bitmap stickers.
concepts.composition: Stacked wide cinematic frames and a video timeline.
concepts.interaction: Animated looping stickers composited onto a clip.
concepts.motion: Tape glitch playback, scrolling frames and audio scratches.
concepts.rationale: Encourages distraction and another video concept instead of the direct collage mechanic.

selection.reason: The grotesque physical objects and fast stacking mechanics are the actual game's identity, not cosmetic skin.

rejected.reason: Fixed radial layout would limit jokes and make precise positioning difficult.
Video framing is too expensive and distracting for quick simultaneous rounds.

tools.reason: All 64 original SVG silhouettes and their composite accessories are written by hand in pieces.js without a separate graphics tool.

assets.role: Main playable library: 64 hand-authored subjects, 5 variants each, 320 total.
assets.acceptance: At 64px tray size, objects are individually recognizable; categories are balanced by server.
assets.integration: The same pieceSVG renderer powers the tray, interactive stage, anonymous gallery and saved SVG export.
assets.provenance: Original geometric SVG paths, no third-party artwork.

assets.acceptance: Three overlapping objects distinguish the icon at 48 pixels.
assets.integration: PWA and favicon use the same asset.

risks: iPhone safe area must never occlude exit
Pointer movement must survive incoming PocketNet state echo
Anonymous gallery must not leak author until reveal
Two-player voting must have meaningful grading
